paper.title: The retirement (food)-consumption puzzle revisited - A panel data study from Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement. The paper states (p. 3, footnote 8): …

registers.name_in_paper: GfK panel services Scandinavia (GfK) / GfK ConsumerScan home-scan household panel
registers.role: outcomes (monthly food purchases: expenditure, quantities, energy, HEI) and questionnaire-based controls; sample frame
variables_mentioned: prices and quantities for all purchased food products (weekly reports)
socio-demographic questionnaire: main shopper, highest education, single or couple household
number of adults eating homemade lunch
days per week the household cooks dinner at home
weekly hours of exercise of the main shopper

registers.name_in_paper: official individual register data at the CPR (central person registration/personal ID number) level from Statistics Denmark
registers.role: treatment (labour market status and the dates of transitions: working, unemployed, disability pension, early voluntary retirement, old age retirement) and linkage
variables_mentioned: labor market status of the individuals in the household
dates of transitions into early voluntary retirement (Efterløn) and old age retirement (Folkepension)

registers.role: controls (number of days per month with hospital or healthcare-center contact, as a proxy for health status; current month and past 6 months)
variables_mentioned: number of days per month with contact with a hospital or healthcare center (routine check-ups for chronic disease, hospitalization admissions, emergency visits; excludes visits to general practitioners)

registers.name_in_paper: register-data measure of annual equalized disposable income
registers.role: controls (proxy for wealth and income shocks: income and income squared)
variables_mentioned: annual equalized disposable income of the household (OECD equivalence scale): salary, profit from own business, property income, public and private pensions and other transfers, interest income and dividends, plus calculated rental value of own house, minus taxes, interest expenses and paid alimony

registers.name_in_paper: Food Composition Databank from the National Food Institute, Technical University of Denmark (https://frida.fooddata.dk/)
registers.role: outcomes (energy and macro-nutrient content per 100 g used to build energy purchased and the HEI)
variables_mentioned: content of energy and macro-nutrients (protein, fat, carbohydrates) per 100 g of each food item

registers.name_in_paper: official 2013 Danish dietary guidelines (The Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, www.altomkost.dk)
registers.role: outcomes (the eight recommendations the HEI scores adherence to)
variables_mentioned: meat from beef, veal, lamb or pork

linkages: GfK purchase data linked to official individual register data at the CPR level from Statistics Denmark; names, addresses and dates of birth were sent from GfK to Statistics Denmark, CPR numbers retrieved and matched, then all identifiers deleted and an anonymous household identifier returned
purchase data concatenated with nutritional data from the Food Composition Databank (DTU) matched at the most detailed product level possible
household members (main shopper and spouse) linked to their individual labour market status and health-contact days in the registers

sample.universe: Danish households in the GfK ConsumerScan panel whose main shopper is at least 55 years old, 2007-2017
selection_rules: 8064 households identified in the data set in the period 2007-2017
delete households where the main shopper is younger than 55 years -> 2620 households
of these, 524 main shoppers retired during the observation period, 1038 had already retired before the start of the observation period and 1058 did not retire

delete households that had retired before being observed; keep households for which the transition into retirement is observed and those that did not retire -> 1582 households with 74,622 monthly observations
378 households retired from employment and 146 retired while outside the labor market
if a household has multiple entries into retirement, the most recent is used
food purchases in months with one or two missing weeks are replaced by the household's average weekly purchases within the same month; months with more than two weeks missing are deleted
estimations run separately for single households (26,841 observations, 639 households) and couple households (42,858 observations, 1044 households)
sample.n_observations: 74,622 monthly observations in the final sample; 26,841 in the single-household estimations and 42,858 in the couple-household estimations
sample.n_individuals: 1582 households (639 single households and 1044 couple households in the estimations)

construction_notes: consumption is expressed per standard individual equivalent: each household member is weighted by gender- and age-dependent recommended daily energy intake relative to a female aged 30-60 (e.g. a male aged 55 has weight 11800/9200 = 1.28)
purchases are aggregated to monthly purchases to limit mismatch between purchase and consumption from storage of staples; purchases and consumption are used interchangeably
around 30 percent of months have one or two weeks without registered purchases; these are imputed with the household's average weekly purchases in the same month

HEI: each of the eight quantifiable 2013 dietary guidelines is scored (s_ij,t - s_ij,0)/(s_ij,recommend - s_ij,0), bounded 0-1, with s_ij,0 at the 99th percentile of observed consumption for adverse foods/nutrients; aggregated with an unweighted Euclidean distance measure (square root of summed squared scores), min 0, max 2.83
guideline quantities are rescaled to household composition and to age- and gender-specific recommended energy intake
retirement = receipt of public pension benefits from early voluntary retirement (Efterløn) or old age retirement (Folkepension); early voluntary and old age retirement are not distinguished

OLM (outside the labor market) definition 1, used in the estimations, covers unemployment benefit, social benefit, disability pension or other types of social support; definition 2 excludes disability pension

lunch-at-home control recoded to 1 if 2 (or 1) or more adults in a couple (or single) household eat lunch at home or a homemade lunchbox, 0.5 if 1 out of 2, 0 otherwise; cooking at home recoded to 1 if the household cooks 5-7 days a week
income enters as annual equalized disposable income per standard person (in 100,000 DKK) and its square
pre-retirement dietary healthiness tau_i = average HEI in the period before retirement; retiring households split 25:50:25 into HEI1 (reference), HEI2, HEI3
older working households of the same type (single or couple) are retained as a control group for time-specific trends

claims.statement: In single-adult households, Retire (retirement from employment) is associated with an increase in HEI (Healthy Eating Index).

treatment.label: Retire (retirement from employment)

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark individual register data linked at CPR level: labour market status (working, unemployed, disability pension, early voluntary retirement, old age retirement) and the dates of these transitions; no register code or variable name given

definition.value: workRet_it: dummy = 1 when the individual who is mainly responsible for shopping has retired from employment, 0 otherwise. Retired is defined as receiving public pension benefits as a result of either early voluntary retirement (Efterlon) or old age retirement (Folkepension); those not retiring from OLM are defined as retiring from work. Early voluntary and old age retirement are not distinguished.

timing.value: from the month of the transition into retirement onwards, within 2007-2017

register_source.value: GfK ConsumerScan / GfK panel services Scandinavia home-scan purchase panel, matched to the Food Composition Databank of the National Food Institute, Technical University of Denmark; no Statistics Denmark register variable named

definition.value: Healthy Eating Index: a combined nutrient and food index of adherence to the eight quantifiable 2013 official Danish dietary guidelines. Each guideline is scored 0-1 per household-month as Score_ij,t = (s_ij,t - s_ij,0)/(s_ij,recommend - s_ij,0), with s_ij,0 set at the 99th percentile of observed consumption for foods/nutrients with adverse health effects; the eight scores are aggregated as the unweighted Euclidean distance HEI_it = sqrt(sum_j score_itj^2), minimum 0 and maximum 2.83. Quantities are recalculated to household size and to age- and gender-specific recommended energy intake.

timing.value: monthly (household-month), 2007-2017; measured before and after the retirement transition

units.value: HEI index points (index scale 0 to 2.83)

magnitude.interpretation: While HEI increases upon retirement, the magnitude is small. The change in HEI ranges from 0.0098-0.024 on a scale from 0 to 2.83

ambiguities: The paper names no estimand for the fixed-effects specification (it names LATE only for the FE-IV estimates in appendix D); ATT is the extractor's reading of a within-household post- versus pre-retirement comparison against a non-retiring control group.

The retirement dummies equal 1 in every month after the transition, so the coefficient is an average over the post-retirement months observed in the 2007-2017 window; the paper states no horizon explicitly.

evidence.how: Table 4 prints Coef., Std. Err. and P>|t| for each column and no confidence interval; no interval is reported anywhere in the paper for this coefficient.

Table 3 prints a second figure in italics under each mean and its title calls them 'std. errors'; with 2057-8664 observations per group a value of 0.23 next to a mean of 2.29 can only be a standard deviation, so it is recorded as the outcome SD with low confidence.

definition.value: Healthy Eating Index: a combined nutrient and food index of adherence to the eight quantifiable 2013 official Danish dietary guidelines. ambiguities: The paper names no estimand for the fixed-effects specification (it names LATE only for the FE-IV estimates in appendix D); ATT is the extractor's reading of a within-household post- versus pre-retirement comparison against a non-retiring control group.

The retirement dummies equal 1 in every month after the transition, so the coefficient is an average over the post-retirement months observed in the 2007-2017 window; the paper states no horizon explicitly.
The spouse variables are described in the text (p. 6) but do not appear in the printed estimating equations (1) and (2), so no parameter symbol is recorded.

evidence.how: Table 5 prints Coef., Std. Err. and P>|t| for each column and no confidence interval; no interval is reported anywhere in the paper for this coefficient.

Table 3 prints pre-retirement means of food expenditure (DKK/month/std.pers.) and energy (MJ/month/std.pers.) in levels, not of the log outcome used here, and prints no efficiency mean at all; no mean of the log outcome is printed and converting the level mean would be our arithmetic, not the paper's number.

ambiguities: The paper names no estimand for the fixed-effects specification (it names LATE only for the FE-IV estimates in appendix D); ATT is the extractor's reading of a within-household post- versus pre-retirement comparison against a non-retiring control group.

The retirement dummies equal 1 in every month after the transition, so the coefficient is an average over the post-retirement months observed in the 2007-2017 window; the paper states no horizon explicitly.
Significance rests on the 10 percent level (P>|t| = 0.0540); statistically_significant is set true because the paper itself reports this coefficient as an effect.
The spouse variables are described in the text (p. 6) but do not appear in the printed estimating equations (1) and (2), so no parameter symbol is recorded.

evidence.how: Table 5 prints Coef., Std. Err. and P>|t| for each column and no confidence interval; no interval is reported anywhere in the paper for this coefficient.

Table 3 prints pre-retirement means of food expenditure (DKK/month/std.pers.) and energy (MJ/month/std.pers.) in levels, not of the log outcome used here, and prints no efficiency mean at all; no mean of the log outcome is printed and converting the level mean would be our arithmetic, not the paper's number.

ambiguities: The paper names no estimand for the fixed-effects specification (it names LATE only for the FE-IV estimates in appendix D); ATT is the extractor's reading of a within-household post- versus pre-retirement comparison against a non-retiring control group.

The retirement dummies equal 1 in every month after the transition, so the coefficient is an average over the post-retirement months observed in the 2007-2017 window; the paper states no horizon explicitly.

evidence.how: Table 5 prints Coef., Std. Err. and P>|t| for each column and no confidence interval; no interval is reported anywhere in the paper for this coefficient.
